questions.question: 'Asthadhyayi', the famous book by Panini is associated to which of the following fields?
questions.solution:
Ashtadhyayi is the foundational text of the grammatical branch of the **Vedanga**.

__
 
• Ashtadhyayi, means eight chapters, **Sanskrit treatise on grammar** written in the 6th to 5th-century BCE by Panini.
 
• It is a prescriptive and generative grammar with algebraic rules governing every aspect of the language. 
 
• It is supplemented by three ancillary texts: *aksarasamamnaya**, dhatupatha,* and *ganapatha*. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Panini **is considered the father of **linguistics **the father of the scientific study of language.
 
• **Panini** gave a comprehensive and scientific theory of **phonetics, phonology, and morphology.**

questions.question: In the preparation of Oxygen by way of decomposition of Potassium Chlorate which chemical compound acts as a catalyst?
questions.solution:
• In the preparation of Oxygen by way of decomposition of Potassium Chlorate,** Manganese dioxide** acts as a catalyst.
 
• Manganese dioxide **(MnO2)** is the **inorganic compound**.
 
• **Potassium chlorate** (KCIO3) is a compound containing potassium, chlorine, and oxygen.
 
• When potassium chlorate (KClO3) is heated in the presence of manganese dioxide as a catalyst, it decomposes to form potassium chloride and oxygen gas.
 
• A catalyst is a substance that causes an increase in the rate of a chemical reaction without being used in the reaction.

questions.question: The defect in image formation for the wandering of the focus on the principal axis of a lens is called ________.
questions.solution:
• **Spherical Aberration **is the defect in image formation for the wandering of the focus on the principal axis of a lens.
 
• Spherical Aberration is a problem that accrued due to the **shape of a spherical lens**
 
• **Astigmatism **is a common vision condition that causes blurred vision. It occurs when the cornea is irregularly shaped or sometimes because of the curvature of the lens inside the eye.
 
• **Chromatic aberration**- In optics, chromatic aberration is a failure of a lens to focus all colours to the same point. It is caused by dispersion.
 
• **Distortion**- Distortion is the alteration of the original shape of any type of signals.

questions.question: Santhali and Khasi belong to the language family of _______.
questions.solution:
• Santhali and Khasi (Spoken Mostly in Meghalaya) are the languages in India that belong to the** Austro-Asiatic** language family.
 
• Austro stands for "**south**" in Greek, so the name Austro-Asiatic.
 
• The languages that belong to this family are mostly spoken in **Southeast Asia**.
 
• The Austro-Asiatic family includes total **168 languages.** 
 
• They are further divided into two branches: **Mon-Khmer **- 147 languages, and **Munda **- 21 languages

questions.question: In a progressive wave, what is the phase difference (in degrees) between two points whose phases are opposite?

questions.question: With respect to Jainism, which of the following words refers to "Achaurya"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Asteya.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Jainism which is also known as Jain Dharma is an ancient Indian Religion.
 
• They trace their history to their twenty-four saviours known as Tirthankars.
 
• The first Tirthankar was Rishabhanatha and the twenty-fourth Tirthankar was Mahavira.
 
• Jain literature is contained in the Agam__ in which a number of Jain texts are there in the Ardha-Maghdi Prakrit language.
 
• **The *five vows* of Jainism are**:

 
• Ahimsa (Non-violence)
 
• Satya (truth)
 
• __**Achaurya or Asteya (non-stealing): **__Not to steal which does not belong to oneself is called __**Achauryanuvrata**__. One is true to his belonging and does not take anything by mistake or intentionally. 
 
• Brahmacharya (Celibacy)
 
• Aparigraha (Non-attachment to temporal possessions)
